newsitem.title: USA: CBOT corn ends mixed, cool forecasts lift new crop.
newsitem.headline: CBOT corn ends mixed, cool forecasts lift new crop.

text.p: New crop corn contracts ended higher Wednesday, lifted by forecasts showing continued cool weather in the U.S. Midwest, floor traders and analysts said.
"The corn is going to need heat to get going," said a floor trader.

Forecasters show that below-normal temperatures are due in the northern Midwest by this weekend. Temperature were seen five to 15 degrees Fahrenheit below normal in some areas, according to private forecaster Weather Services Corp.
Most of the corn crop has been planted, but some said that warm weather is needed to spur growth.
However, others said that temperatures have been steadily climbing since most of the crop was planted, so no danger from cool weather was seen.

"You can't hurt corn this early even if it's emerged," said Sid Love, grain analyst with Kropf and Love consulting. "It's the soil temperature that really matters, and its due to warm up as far as I can see."
Commodity funds selling as well as profit taking on bull spreads hit the old crop corn contracts, traders said.
CBOT wheat settled one to 2-1/2 cents per bushel higher, with July wheat up 1-3/4 at $4.04-1/4 per bushel.
On the day, FIMAT Futures Inc sold seven million bushels July and Goldenberg Hehmeyer sold four million bushels July.
O'Connor Grain bought five million July and Iowa Grain bought two million July and one million bushels December, pit traders said.
In spread trade, Cargill spread two million July/May, Continental Grain spread two million September/December and Cargill Investor Services spread two million July/May, pit traders said.
In options trading, Prudential Securities bought 400 July $3.10 calls and sold 400 July $2.70 puts. Tenco Inc bought 400 July $3.20 calls, pit traders said.
Volume was estimated at 70,000 contracts. That figure is lower than Tuesday's final volume of 98,527 contracts, according to CBOT data.
